analysis:
The only change in scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py is at head lines 141-142. It adds "model-requant-upload.yml" to the UNROUTED tuple, so the repository's CI test now classifies that workflow as credentialed or release-class. The change is test-only and touches no provider runtime, key custody, attestation, or cache code. T-041 is the only supplied threat definition and it is unrelated to this file.

The addition tightens the CI guard. test_every_workflow_is_classified requires every workflow file to be classified. test_release_and_credentialed_workflows_keep_literal_runners (lines 924-943) requires unrouted workflows to avoid darkbloom-route.yml and needs.route, and requires every runs-on to match ^blacksmith-[a-z0-9-]+$. It also forbids the self-hosted and darkbloom-* labels. The watchdog test (lines 963-966) additionally requires that unrouted workflows never carry darkbloom labels or self-hosted.

With this change, a model-requant-upload.yml that runs on a self-hosted Darkbloom runner or reads the route output would fail CI. That prevents credentialed model upload and requantization from running on the sandbox-plane runners. This is a security-positive control, not a regression.

The workflow file itself is not in the supplied evidence. Whether it actually has literal Blacksmith runners, and whether it holds secrets, is unverified. If it was added in the same PR, this test will enforce the property. No finding is raised. Other batch files were not examined.
